solutions.latex:
$A=49$ cm$^2$, $A=\dfrac12r^2\theta$, so $49=\dfrac12r^2\theta$, $98=r^2\theta$ and $\theta=\dfrac{98}{r^2}$.

Arc length $l=r\theta=r\times\dfrac{98}{r^2}=\dfrac{98}{r}$.

Perimeter $P=r+r+\dfrac{98}{r}=2r+98r^{-1}$.

$$\dfrac{dP}{dr}=2-98r^{-2}=2-\dfrac{98}{r^2},\qquad \dfrac{d^2P}{dr^2}=196r^{-3}=\dfrac{196}{r^3}$$

Stationary point when $\dfrac{dP}{dr}=0$: $2-\dfrac{98}{r^2}=0$, $\dfrac{98}{r^2}=2$, $r^2=49$, $r=7$ as $r>0$.

Nature of the stationary point when $r=7$: $\dfrac{d^2P}{dr^2}=\dfrac{196}{7^3}>0$, so a minimum value.

$\therefore$ minimum perimeter occurs when $r=7$ cm, $d=14$ cm.

$l=r\theta$ where $r=7$ and $\theta=\dfrac{98}{r^2}=\dfrac{98}{7^2}$, so $l=7\times\dfrac{98}{7^2}=\dfrac{98}{7}=14$ cm $=2\times r=$ diameter.

So the minimum perimeter occurs when the arc length is equal to the diameter.

solutions.latex:
$f'(x)=\dfrac{\mu-x}{\sigma^2}f(x)$. Let $u=\dfrac{\mu-x}{\sigma^2}$, $v=f(x)$; then $u'=-\dfrac1{\sigma^2}$, $v'=f'(x)=\dfrac{\mu-x}{\sigma^2}f(x)$.

$$\begin{aligned}f''(x)&=u\,v'+v\,u'\\&=\dfrac{\mu-x}{\sigma^2}\times\dfrac{\mu-x}{\sigma^2}f(x)+f(x)\left(-\dfrac1{\sigma^2}\right)\\&=\dfrac{(\mu-x)^2}{\sigma^4}f(x)-\dfrac{f(x)}{\sigma^2}\\&=\dfrac{f(x)}{\sigma^2}\left[\dfrac{(\mu-x)^2}{\sigma^2}-1\right]\end{aligned}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: correct solution; 1: using the product rule and making some progress towards $f''(x)$ or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
$f''(x)=0$ for inflection points:

$$\dfrac{f(x)}{\sigma^2}\left[\dfrac{(\mu-x)^2}{\sigma^2}-1\right]=0$$

$\dfrac{f(x)}{\sigma^2}\ne0$ as $f(x)\ne0$, so $\dfrac{(\mu-x)^2}{\sigma^2}-1=0$, $(\mu-x)^2=\sigma^2$, $\mu-x=\pm\sigma$, $x-\mu=\pm\sigma$, so $x=\mu\pm\sigma$.

So $x$ lies one standard deviation either side of the mean.

$M_n=0$ when all money runs out:

$$0=3\,000\,000-(3\,000\,000-1\,684\,222.89)(1.003)^n$$

$$1\,315\,777.11(1.003)^n=3\,000\,000\Rightarrow(1.003)^n=\dfrac{3\,000\,000}{1\,315\,777.11}$$

$$n\ln(1.003)=\ln\left(\dfrac{3\,000\,000}{1\,315\,777.11}\right)\Rightarrow n=\dfrac{\ln\left(\frac{3\,000\,000}{1\,315\,777.11}\right)}{\ln(1.003)}=275.14\text{ months}$$

This is one month short of 23 years. So Rylie will run out of money one month before his 90th birthday.

solutions.latex:
$y=x^2e^x$. Let $u=x^2$, $v=e^x$: $y'=2xe^x+x^2e^x=xe^x(2+x)$.

$y''=2e^x+2xe^x+2xe^x+x^2e^x=e^x(2+4x+x^2)$.

Stationary points $y'=0$: $0=xe^x(2+x)$, so $x=0$, $e^x=0$ (does not exist), or $2+x=0$; hence $x=0$ or $x=-2$.

When $x=0$, $y=0$: $(0,0)$. When $x=-2$, $y=\dfrac4{e^2}$: $\left(-2,\dfrac4{e^2}\right)$.

Classify: $x=0$: $y''=1(2+0)>0$, concave up, so minimum point $(0,0)$. $x=-2$: $y''=e^{-2}(2-8+4)<0$, concave down, so maximum point $\left(-2,\dfrac4{e^2}\right)$.

Inflections $y''=0$: $0=e^x(2+4x+x^2)$; $e^x=0$ (does not exist) or $x^2+4x+2=0$, so

$$x=\dfrac{-4\pm\sqrt{4^2-4\times1\times2}}{2}=\dfrac{-4\pm2\sqrt2}{2}=-2\pm\sqrt2$$

Concavity test: for $x=-1,-0.6,0$ the sign of $y''$ is $<0,0,>0$, so concavity changes; for $x=-4,-3.4,-1$ the sign of $y''$ is $>0,0,<0$, so concavity changes. Therefore both are inflections.
